name: UNC2717
iocPatterns: Web shells on network edge devices ", "Evidence clearing (log wipers)
keyCapabilities: Exploitation of zero-day and known vulnerabilities in VPN appliances
Persistence via firmware manipulation and rollback partition injection
Sophisticated web shell development with multi-layered functionality
Advanced anti-forensics including log suppression and evidence removal
Credential harvesting from memory (LSASS) and local databases (LMDB)
Automated housekeeping to hide presence during system upgrades
MFA bypass via modification of authentication logic
recommendedActions: Patch all perimeter network devices, especially Pulse Secure and Ivanti, to mitigate known vulnerabilities.
Conduct immediate audits for web shells on all internet-facing hardware (firmware analysis).
Implement File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) specifically for core libraries like libdsplibs.so and system scripts.
Scan network appliances for hidden shell entries in non-standard directories or rollback partitions.
Monitor and alert on any process's interaction with LSASS memory outside of standard authentication events.
Implement log aggregation to a secure remote server to prevent local-only log deletion from hiding activity.
Perform forensic imaging of compromised gateways before performing reboots to preserve evidence in volatile memory.
Rotate all credentials used on systems accessed via VPN or managed through compromise sites.
campaignsText: UNC2711 and its closely related affiliate UNC2630 have operated since at least 2018/2019. They participate in long-term campaigns targeting high-value infrastructure to facilitate the theft of intellectual property useful for both commercial and military applications. A notable campaign window occurred from late 2020 through early 2021, where they heavily exploited Pulse Secure appliances to breach government agencies and defense contractors. The group has demonstrated an evolution toward more sophisticated anti-forensics, shifting from standard web shells to advanced firmware-level modifications that ensure persistence during system upgrades.
description: UNC2717 is a highly sophisticated Chinese-sponsored threat actor specializing in compromising networking infrastructure (notably Pulse Secure VPN appliances) to facilitate long-term espionage. The group utilizes advanced anti-forensics, firmware manipulation, and custom web shells to steal credentials and intellectual property from government, defense, and critical infrastructure sectors.
goals: UNC2717's strategic objectives are primarily driven by Chinese national interests, focusing on intellectual property theft and intelligence gathering. Their target profile is expansive but specific: they prioritize high-value industries including defense, aerospace, government agencies, manufacturing (specifically those involving advanced technology), and critical infrastructure like transportation and energy. While their operations involve a broad geographic scope, there is evidence of prioritized targeting against entities providing sensitive data related to military technology such as Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs).
